rv.q: Each passage turns the few minutes between post time and the finish line into an existential thriller, guaranteed to leave one breathless with suspense.
SMALL is a 100 minutes of a lush, embraceable story told by a dancer/actor who embodies with ease and art all of the remarkable real life characters who inhabit the world of horse racing.
Small is a unique and engaging show from someone who has been there and knows how to recreate this milieu.
A fun-size burst of joy, Montano is a magnetic storyteller, and director Jessi D. Hill builds off that with a production that complements Montano’s natural gifts.
Montano is an ingratiating and thoroughly engaging storyteller.
Life comes with huge twists of fate, and SMALL offers a worthwhile reminder.
Small lifts you into the saddle and challenges you to hang on for a bumpy but exhilarating ride.
IT’S LIKE READING A LONG SECTION OF TEXT THAT’S IN ALL CAPS, BECAUSE WHEN EVERYTHING IS IN ALL CAPS, IT LOSES ITS IMPACT AND ONLY FEELS RELENTLESS AND LOUD.

cn.t: Robert Montano's solo show earns praise for its tour-de-force performance and pulse-pounding storytelling about his teenage dream of becoming a jockey, with critics lauding the fully integrated theatrical elements that create an exciting, polished gem.
